properties.corrosion_resistance: Excellent — resistant to phosphoric acid, seawater, halogens at moderate temps

disassembly_notes: Non-sparking cut with carbide tools. Separate from carbon steel before binning — mixed contamination downgrades to Class B. XRF verification recommended for high-value recovery.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Outstanding — seawater, acids, alkalis, high temp oxidation to 980°C

disassembly_notes: HIGH VALUE — segregate immediately into dedicated Inconel bin. Do not mix with other Ni alloys (Inconel 718, Hastelloy) without XRF verification. Recovery value strongly justifies Grade A certification.

AEROSPACE GRADE. Verify part life limit status before recovery routing — life-expired titanium must be mutilated per FAA AC 20-62E and cannot re-enter parts supply chain. Non-life-expired Ti warrants certified scrap value.

properties.chemical_resistance: Exceptional — resistant to virtually all chemicals

disassembly_notes: Low recovery value. Do NOT incinerate — at high temps PTFE releases perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a persistent pollutant. Thermal processing at licensed fluoropolymer facility only. Bin as Class-C polymer.

Common valve and pump body material. Do not mix with stainless steel — density sensors and XRF will catch contamination. Carbon steel scrap value ~$0.25/kg vs 316L at $1.42/kg — segregation is important for revenue capture.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Superior — hydrochloric acid, chlorine, wet chlorine gas, hypochlorite, chlorine dioxide solutions

disassembly_notes: HIGH VALUE Ni-Mo-Cr alloy. XRF mandatory before binning — easily confused with Inconel without testing. Segregate into dedicated Hastelloy bin, do not contaminate with 625 or 718 grade alloys. Scrap buyer will require mill cert confirmation.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Excellent pitting and crevice corrosion resistance, superior to 316L in chloride environments

disassembly_notes: Duplex SS commands premium over standard austenitic grades. Must be separated from 316L and carbon steel — grades are visually identical, XRF is the only reliable differentiator. Bin as high-grade SS scrap. Do not cut with carbon steel tools without cleaning.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Exceptional — subsea, aggressive chloride, sour gas service. PREN > 43

disassembly_notes: Higher value than standard duplex. Common in offshore and subsea valve bodies. XRF verify before routing — PREN value test distinguishes from 2205. Keep separate from lower-grade stainless scrap. Hydrogen embrittlement risk if improperly stored.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Good — natural oxide layer. Avoid contact with copper alloys (galvanic corrosion)

disassembly_notes: Lightweight, high recyclability. Keep separate from other aluminium alloys (2xxx, 7xxx series) — different recovery specs. Do not bin with steel; magnetic separation effective. Avoid contamination with paint, coatings, or anodising compounds before smelting.

HIGH VALUE — copper scrap is a priority revenue stream. Segregate immediately from brass, bronze, and copper alloys — blended copper downgrades significantly. Strip insulation before binning (bare copper vs insulated copper differ by ~$1.50/kg). No flux or solder contamination.

Common in marine valve trim, pump impellers, and fittings. Keep separate from pure copper — brass alloys command lower scrap price. Lead content may be present in free-machining variants (confirm with XRF). Route as Red Brass scrap category.

properties.corrosion_resistance: Excellent — hydrofluoric acid, seawater, salt solutions, alkaline solutions

disassembly_notes: High value Ni-Cu alloy used in pump shafts, valve trim, and marine fasteners. Visually similar to stainless — XRF mandatory. Segregate into Monel-specific bin. Do not mix with Inconel or pure nickel alloys without XRF confirmation.

Standard forged carbon steel for flanges, fittings, and valve bodies. Slightly higher value than cast WCB grades due to forged grain structure. Magnetic — easy to separate from SS with magnet test. Bin as heavy melting scrap (HMS1).

Common in older pump housings, compressor blocks, and valve bodies. Low recovery value but high recyclability as foundry return. Brittle — do not drop, risk of shattering and creating sharp shards (PPE required). Bin separately from nodular/ductile iron (different metallurgy).
